caption:
The Louvre Pyramid doesn't actually have 666 panes despite what The Da Vinci Code claims — and the rooster on top of Notre-Dame is secretly a reliquary. 👀

Comment your guess for which fact surprised you most before you swipe ⬇️

1. Louvre Pyramid
The Da Vinci Code made "666 panes" famous, but I.M. Pei's Louvre Pyramid actually has 673 glass panes — 603 diamonds and 70 triangles, confirmed by the architect's own team.

2. Sainte-Chapelle
Sainte-Chapelle's 13th-century windows pack in 1,113 biblical scenes across 618 square meters of glass — and most survived WWII only because they were pulled out pane by pane and hidden.

3. Notre-Dame
Notre-Dame's gilded spire rooster secretly holds fragments of the Crown of Thorns. It survived the 2019 fire even as the spire collapsed beneath it.

4. The Panthéon
In 1851, Léon Foucault hung a 28kg bob from a 67-meter wire under the Panthéon's dome — the first visual proof the planet rotates. You can still watch it swing today.

5. Palais Garnier
Beneath the Paris Opera House sits a 25x50 meter underground reservoir Charles Garnier built to fight groundwater — the real inspiration for Phantom of the Opera. Fire divers still train in it.

6. The Catacombs
The Paris Catacombs hold the bones of roughly 6 million people — more than double the city's living population — packed into tunnels it took 12 years to fill.

7. Shakespeare and Company
Since 1951, over 30,000 traveling writers have slept for free among the shelves at Shakespeare and Company — in exchange for reading one book a day.
